title: The standard t-structure on the integral category
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and chosen uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be a noetherian scheme of finite dimension on which $\ell$ is invertible. Put $P_n=A/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$ and $A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$, the completed coefficient sheaf of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and write
$$
 D=D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T)),\qquad \mathcal C=\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)\subset D
$$
for the full bounded constructible complete category, including compatible etale-origin witnesses, of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. Let $\mathcal H^i$ denote the ambient cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Set
$$
 \mathcal C^{\leq0}=\{K\in\mathcal C:\mathcal H^i(K)=0\text{ for all }i>0\},\qquad
 \mathcal C^{\geq0}=\{K\in\mathcal C:\mathcal H^i(K)=0\text{ for all }i<0\}.
$$
With the inherited shift and distinguished triangles, these form a bounded t-structure [def-weil-t-structure] on $\mathcal C$. Its truncation functors are the restrictions of the canonical ambient truncations $\tau_D^{\leq m}$ and $\tau_D^{\geq m}$ for every $m\in\mathbf Z$, with their canonical maps and triangles; its heart consists exactly of the objects whose ambient cohomology sheaves vanish in every degree other than zero.

For any $K\in\mathcal C$ satisfying the Tor-compatibility hypothesis of [thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations] at every level of its normalized reduction tower $K_n=K\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T$, these same canonical truncations are the derived limits of the levelwise truncated towers specified in that theorem, with its canonical reduction isomorphisms and normalization compatibility. The general t-structure assertion does not impose this additional hypothesis on every object.

An object is called $\varpi$-power-torsion here if $\varpi^N\operatorname{id}_K=0$ in $\mathcal C$ for some integer $N\geq1$, using the scalar endomorphisms induced by multiplication on complexes of $A_T$-modules. Both truncation functors preserve this condition with the same exponent: for every such $K,N$ and every $m\in\mathbf Z$,
$$
 \varpi^N\operatorname{id}_{\tau^{\leq m}K}=0,\qquad
 \varpi^N\operatorname{id}_{\tau^{\geq m}K}=0.
$$

$\tau_{\le a}K^\bullet\to K^\bullet\to\tau_{\ge a+1}K^\bullet\to(\tau_{\le a}K^\bullet)[1]$
of a complex of an abelian category, Remark 13.12.4 ([Tag
08J5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08J5)) with Section 12.15 ([Tag

standard t-structure on the derived complete category, its identification
with the truncations of [thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations] and the
stability of the $\varpi$-power-torsion subcategory.

proof.text: Work throughout in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$, not the derived category of modules over the constant sheaf $\underline A$. By [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], $\mathcal C$ is full and its morphisms are all the ambient morphisms between its objects. By [lem-weil-pbc-uniform-complete-triangulated] it is triangulated with inherited shifts and triangles and exact inclusion. By [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], cohomology is that of this same completed coefficient sheaf. The last sentence of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] puts $\tau_D^{\leq m}K$ and $\tau_D^{\geq m}K$ in $\mathcal C$ for every $K\in\mathcal C$ and every $m$. Its hypotheses are exactly our finite coefficient extension, noetherian finite-dimensional $T$, and invertibility of $\ell$. This use includes the compatible etale-origin witnesses explicitly retained by that statement. It supplies unrestricted ambient truncation closure; the Tor-conditional tower construction is not used here.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11 and Proposition 6.8.11(3), applied through the cited completed-coefficient characterization; blueprint proof, first two sentences

proof.text: Apply [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] to the abelian category $\operatorname{Mod}(A_T)$. Its nonpositive and nonnegative classes, intersected with $\mathcal C$, are exactly the two displayed classes. They are strictly full since cohomology preserves isomorphisms. The ambient shift conditions restrict to them because the shifts of $\mathcal C$ are inherited: $\mathcal C^{\leq0}[1]\subseteq\mathcal C^{\leq0}$ and $\mathcal C^{\geq0}[-1]\subseteq\mathcal C^{\geq0}$. For $X\in\mathcal C^{\leq0}$ and $Y\in\mathcal C^{\geq0}$, fullness identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,Y[-1])$ with the ambient Hom group, which is zero by the ambient t-structure. These are the first two axioms of [def-weil-t-structure].

source.place: Definition 1.3.1 and Example 1.3.2(i); blueprint proof, shift conditions and orthogonality

proof.text:
For $K\in\mathcal C$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$, apply [lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle] with $b=m+1$ in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$. It gives the distinguished triangle
$$
 \tau_D^{\leq m}K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow\tau_D^{\geq m+1}K\longrightarrow(\tau_D^{\leq m}K)[1]
$$
whose first term has no cohomology above $m$ and whose third term has none below $m+1$. Both terms belong to $\mathcal C$ by the truncation-closure clause of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. This triangle is distinguished in $\mathcal C$ by the inherited-triangle assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-uniform-complete-triangulated]. For $m=0$ write its third term as $B[-1]$, where $B=(\tau_D^{\geq1}K)[1]\in\mathcal C^{\geq0}$ by the ambient shift convention already used. This proves the third axiom of [def-weil-t-structure]. Together with Step 2 it proves the t-structure on all of $\mathcal C$, without an extra flatness assumption.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle (canonical truncation triangle), with homology.tex Tag 0118, section-truncations; blueprint proof, truncation axiom

proof.text: Condition (iii) of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], applied to $K\in\mathcal C$, says in particular that $K$ is bounded. Choose integers $a\leq b$ with $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$, choosing $a=b=0$ when $K=0$. The shifted classes are the intersections with the ambient degree bounds, so $K\in\mathcal C^{\geq a}\cap\mathcal C^{\leq b}$. This is boundedness in [def-weil-t-structure]. Its definition of the heart as $\mathcal C^{\leq0}\cap\mathcal C^{\geq0}$ gives precisely vanishing in all degrees other than zero, by intersecting the two defining conditions. No assertion about finite generation of section groups, or about a finite-type-over-a-field presentation of $T$, is required.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3); blueprint proof, boundedness sentence; heart by Definition 1.3.1 of BBD

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1), a triangle with these degree bounds gives the canonical truncations uniquely, and the lower and upper truncations are right and left adjoint to the respective full inclusions. Thus the triangles of Step 3 identify the truncation objects with the restrictions of $\tau_D^{\leq m}$ and $\tau_D^{\geq m+1}$. Fullness in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] makes their canonical maps morphisms in $\mathcal C$. To check the functors, let $f:K\to L$. The ambient lower truncation map satisfies
$$
 \epsilon_L\,\tau_D^{\leq m}(f)=f\epsilon_K.
$$
The lower adjunction makes it the unique map with this equation, so it is also the integral lower truncation map. For the upper truncation, its ambient map satisfies
$$
 \tau_D^{\geq m+1}(f)\eta_K=\eta_L f,
$$
The upper adjunction identifies maps out of the upper truncation with maps out of the original object into this nonnegative target; hence this equation uniquely specifies the upper truncation map in the full subcategory. These equations prove naturality of the identifications and compatibility with the canonical units and counits. Replacing $m+1$ by an arbitrary integer gives the asserted upper functor for all cutoffs.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i),(ii), adjunctions and uniqueness of truncation triangles; blueprint proof, identification of truncation functors

proof.text: Now let $K\in\mathcal C$ satisfy precisely the all-level Tor-compatibility hypothesis of [thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations]. That theorem supplies its two derived-limit truncation objects, the canonical reduction isomorphisms compatible with normalization, and their identification with the ambient canonical truncations. The latter are the integral truncations by Step 5. Hence the theorem's derived-limit descriptions and reduction maps compute these same integral truncations on its stated domain. The uniqueness assertion of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1) identifies their canonical triangles. For morphisms within this domain, the two unit/counit equations in Step 5 determine the truncation maps uniquely, so the comparison is natural there. This does not assert that every integral object satisfies the tower theorem's Tor hypothesis.

source.place: Statement, explicit Tor hypothesis, clauses (i)--(iii) and coincidence with ambient canonical truncations; repaired scope of the adjacent integral-tstructure proposition

proof.text: Here is the scalar compatibility needed for the last clause, without assuming linearity merely from additivity. For $r\in A$, its compatible residues define a section of $A_T$ by the pointwise limit-ring construction in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Multiplication by that section in each degree is a chain endomorphism $r_C$ of every complex of $A_T$-modules, and every module chain map satisfies $fr_C=r_{C'}f$. The localization description of $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] implies the same equality for every derived morphism: it holds for the images of chain maps. For a quasi-isomorphism $q:C\to C'$, the equation $qr_C=r_{C'}q$ gives $r_Cq^{-1}=q^{-1}r_{C'}$ after multiplication on the left and right by $q^{-1}$. The equation is preserved under composition; the images of chain maps and these inverses generate the localized morphisms. Thus multiplication gives a central scalar endomorphism $r_K=r\operatorname{id}_K$ on every object of $\mathcal C$ with the same commutation equation.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: explicit verification of the scalar compatibility used for uniformizer torsion

proof.text:
Fix $r=\varpi^N$ with $N\geq1$ and suppose $r_K=0$. Put $U=\tau^{\leq m}K$ and $V=\tau^{\geq m}K$, with canonical maps $\epsilon:U\to K$ and $\eta:K\to V$. Step 7 gives
$$
 \epsilon r_U=r_K\epsilon=0,\qquad r_V\eta=\eta r_K=0.
$$
Since $U\in\mathcal C^{\leq m}$, the lower adjunction in [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1) makes $\operatorname{Hom}(U,U)\to\operatorname{Hom}(U,K)$, $h\mapsto\epsilon h$, bijective. It sends $r_U$ and $0$ to the same morphism, so $r_U=0$. Since $V\in\mathcal C^{\geq m}$, the upper adjunction makes $\operatorname{Hom}(V,V)\to\operatorname{Hom}(K,V)$, $h\mapsto h\eta$, bijective; it sends both $r_V$ and $0$ to the zero morphism by the second displayed equation. Its injectivity gives $r_V=0$. This proves torsion stability with the original exponent, including for nonflat torsion objects.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i), adjunction injectivity, applied to the central scalar action; blueprint proof, final torsion clause

blueprint_update.statement:
In the setting of [thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations], set
$$
 (\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A))^{\le0}:=\{K:\mathcal H^i(K)=0\ \forall i>0\},
$$
$$
 (\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A))^{\ge0}:=\{K:\mathcal H^i(K)=0\ \forall i<0\}.
$$
These form a bounded t-structure on $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$, whose truncation
functors are the $\tau^{\le m},\tau^{\ge m}$ of
[thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations] and whose heart consists of the objects
with cohomology concentrated in degree zero. The subcategory of
$\varpi$-power-torsion objects is stable under the truncation functors.

proof.text:
The shift conditions and the orthogonality of a t-structure, namely
$\Hom(A,B[-1])=0$ for $A\in(\Dbc)^{\le0}$, $B\in(\Dbc)^{\ge0}$, are the
corresponding ambient statements for the standard t-structure of
$D(T_{\Proet},A)$, since $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$ is a full subcategory and its
objects' cohomology sheaves are the ambient ones. The truncation axiom and
the truncation triangles are [thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations] (ii)--(iii)
with the cohomology formulas of (ii) showing the end terms to lie in the
claimed subcategories. Boundedness: by the reconstruction lemma for uniform
towers (and its use in [thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations]), an object's
local models are supported in a finite interval $[d_0,d_1]$, so its
cohomology vanishes outside it; the interval is part of the data of
[def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. Finally the truncation
functors are additive and $A_T$-linear, so if $\varpi^n\cdot1_K=0$ in
$\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$, then
$\varpi^n\cdot1_{\tau^{\le m}K}=\tau^{\le m}(\varpi^n\cdot1_K)=0$, and
similarly for $\tau^{\ge m+1}$.
